# pinboard-xr

**Spatial Focus & AI Sticky Notes**: a mixed-reality pinboard for **Meta Quest 3S** with a Pomodoro timer and sticky notes generated by models running locally on your Mac (**Ollama** or **MUSE** / any OpenAI-compatible server).

Built with Vite, React 19, TypeScript, `@react-three/fiber` 9, `@react-three/xr` 6, `@react-three/handle` 6 and `@react-three/drei` 10.

## Features

- **Passthrough AR**: transparent canvas plus `store.enterAR()`, so your real room stays visible.
- **Control dock** (at `[0, 1.25, -0.75]`):
  - **+ New Note** adds a template note.
  - **Voice / AI Note** uses Web Speech to take a spoken thought and turns it into 1–5 actionable notes.
  - **AI Summarize Board** adds an action-plan note.
  - **Start / Pause / Reset** runs a 25-minute Pomodoro.
  - **Provider toggle** switches between Ollama and MUSE.
- **Sticky notes**: pinch (hands), grab (controllers) or mouse-drag (desktop) to place them. Each note has buttons to **cycle color** (yellow → cyan → pink), **AI Expand** (adds 3 sub-steps beside it) and **×** to delete. On desktop, double-click a note to edit it.
- **Pomodoro card**: draggable, with a progress bar and a chime when the timer finishes.
- Notes, their positions, the timer-card position and your provider/model settings are saved in the browser's `localStorage`.
- Crisp text: every label is drawn on a high-DPI HTML canvas and mapped onto a 3D plane. No 3D UI library is used.

## 1. Setup (macOS Terminal)

```bash
cd ~/Desktop/code/AI/pinboard-xr
npm install
cp .env.example .env        # then edit model names / ports
brew install mkcert         # recommended (see the HTTPS note below)
npm run dev
```

Requires Node 20.19+ (`node -v`). All versions are pinned in `package.json`, and `npm install` needs no `--legacy-peer-deps`.

`.env` keys:

| Key | Used by | Default |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `VITE_AI_PROVIDER` | browser | `ollama` (or `muse`) |
| `VITE_OLLAMA_MODEL` | browser | `llama3.2` |
| `VITE_MUSE_MODEL` | browser | `muse` |
| `OLLAMA_URL` | Vite proxy only | `http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1` |
| `MUSE_URL` | Vite proxy only | `http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1` |
| `MKCERT_PATH` | Vite (optional) | auto-detects Homebrew `mkcert` |

You can change the provider and model later in the 2D overlay (they're saved per browser). Restart `npm run dev` after changing `OLLAMA_URL` or `MUSE_URL`.

### How the AI proxy works

The Quest loads the app from `https://<MAC_IP>:5173`. A direct `fetch()` from that HTTPS page to `http://<MAC_IP>:11434` would be blocked as mixed content (and by CORS). Instead, the browser calls the same HTTPS origin, and Vite forwards the request to your Mac's local servers:

```
https://<MAC_IP>:5173/api/ollama/chat/completions  ->  http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/chat/completions
https://<MAC_IP>:5173/api/muse/chat/completions    ->  http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/chat/completions
```

The proxy also removes the browser's `Origin` header, so Ollama doesn't reject the request with HTTP 403. You don't need to set `OLLAMA_ORIGINS` or `OLLAMA_HOST`: Ollama can stay bound to `127.0.0.1`.

## 2. Verify the local models

### Ollama

```bash
ollama serve                      # skip if the Ollama menu-bar app is already running
ollama pull llama3.2              # or any chat model, e.g. qwen3:8b, gemma3
curl http://127.0.0.1:11434/v1/models
lsof -nP -iTCP:11434 -sTCP:LISTEN # shows the process listening on 11434
```

### MUSE (or LM Studio / llama.cpp / vLLM)

Find the port the server is listening on, then check that it serves the OpenAI API:

```bash
lsof -nP -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN | grep -Ei 'muse|python|lms|llama|node'
curl http://127.0.0.1:8000/v1/models    # try 1234 (LM Studio) or 8080 (llama.cpp) if 8000 fails
```

Put the working base URL (with `/v1`) in `.env` as `MUSE_URL`, set `VITE_MUSE_MODEL` to one of the listed model ids, and restart `npm run dev`.

Then open `https://localhost:5173` on the Mac and click **Test connection** in the Local AI card. The **Pick…** menu lists the models the server reports.

## 3. Connect the Quest 3S

1. Put the Mac and the Quest on the **same Wi-Fi network**.
2. Find the Mac's IP address:
   ```bash
   ipconfig getifaddr en0     # Wi-Fi; try en1 if this prints nothing
   ```
   `npm run dev` also prints it under `Network:`.
3. On the Quest, open **Meta Quest Browser** and go to `https://<MAC_IP>:5173` (include the `https://` and the port).
4. The browser warns that the connection isn't private, because the mkcert certificate is trusted on your Mac but not on the headset. Choose **Advanced**, then **Proceed to <MAC_IP> (unsafe)**. You only need to do this once per certificate.
5. Press **Enter Mixed Reality** and allow the permissions the browser asks for.
6. Point with a controller ray or your hand, then pull the trigger or pinch to press buttons. Pinch or grab a note's paper to move it.

### Troubleshooting

- **The page doesn't load on the Quest**: check that the IP and port are right, that both devices are on the same network (guest networks often block device-to-device traffic), and that the macOS firewall allows incoming connections for `node`.
- **`npm run dev` fails with an mkcert or GitHub error**: run `brew install mkcert`. The config uses the Homebrew binary automatically, so the plugin doesn't need to download one from GitHub (which can be rate-limited).
- **"Proxy could not reach …" in the dock**: the model server isn't running, or `OLLAMA_URL` / `MUSE_URL` points to the wrong port.
- **HTTP 404 "model not found"**: the model name doesn't match what the server reports. Use **Pick…** in the overlay.
- **Voice doesn't work in the headset**: Quest Browser may not support Web Speech, especially in an immersive session. The button then uses the "Voice fallback" thought you set in the overlay (cycling through presets). On desktop you're asked to type the thought instead.
- **Answers are slow**: the first request after loading a model can take a while. The proxy waits up to 180 seconds.

## Desktop testing (no headset needed)

Open **`https://localhost:5173`** in Chrome on the Mac. Use `localhost`, not the IP address: the emulator only loads on localhost.

- **Desktop preview**: a simple 3D view. Drag the background to orbit and scroll to zoom. Click the 3D buttons, drag notes and the timer card with the mouse, and double-click a note to edit it.
- **Enter Mixed Reality (emulator)**: when no headset is connected, this button loads Meta's IWER emulator, a virtual Quest 3 in a simulated living room that stands in for passthrough. That gives you a real immersive-ar session with the same code path as the headset:
  - Drag in the scene to look around. The toolbar at the top switches between controllers and hands, and has the exit button.
  - Move a controller with its gizmo or the side panel. Its ray hits whatever it points at.
  - Press **RT/LT (trigger)** in the controller panel to click a button. Hold the trigger while moving the controller to drag a note.
  - Exit the session from the toolbar to return to the overlay.

Your notes and settings are shared between the preview and the emulator.

## Project structure

```
vite.config.ts                     HTTPS (mkcert) + /api/ollama & /api/muse proxies
src/main.tsx                       React entry
src/App.tsx                        Canvas, XR store, scene, desktop helpers
src/services/localAiClient.ts      OpenAI-compatible client (models, chat, parsing, errors)
src/services/speech.ts             Web Speech API wrapper with typed errors
src/store/useSpatialStore.ts       Zustand store: notes, timer, provider, AI/voice actions
src/utils/canvasTexture.ts         High-DPI canvas → texture drawing + hook
src/utils/desktopEmulator.ts       Quest 3 emulator for testing on a Mac without a headset
src/components/Button3D.tsx        Pressable 3D button
src/components/ControlDock.tsx     Floating dock with status line
src/components/StickyNote.tsx      Draggable note with color / AI Expand / delete
src/components/PomodoroCard.tsx    Draggable 25-minute timer card
src/components/LandingOverlay.tsx  2D landing page, AI settings, voice fallback
```

Scripts: `npm run dev`, `npm run build` (type-check and production build), `npm run preview`, `npm run typecheck`.
